Lessons.Title: Division Game Day
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will develop fluency with dividing within 100.
In this lesson, you continue to develop fluency with dividing whole numbers within 100 by playing games. You should have an efficient strategy for finding quotients, but you do not need to know quotients from memory.
Warm-up Number Talk: mentally divide 48 by 2, 3, 4 and 6, obtaining 24, 16, 12 and 8. Discuss the related multiplication facts for 48.

Activity 1 Race to 1. On the first turn roll a number cube for a divisor (reroll if 5), choose a number from 12, 16, 18 or 24, divide and record an expression and quotient. On later turns choose either a previous quotient or a fresh starter number; reroll 5, divide and record. First to obtain quotient 1 wins. The source presents a table and a sample, not a fixed synthetic game outcome.

Activity 2 Compare, Division. Two partners split independent quotient-expression cards and reveal a card each turn. The higher value wins both cards. At the end the player with more cards wins. Verify quotient comparisons using multiplication when useful.

Independent practice path (not the publisher's completed game): start at 12, divide by 3 to get 4, then divide that previous quotient by 4 to reach 1. Teachers must ensure learners explain how a chosen source game is legitimately played.
Lesson synthesis reflects on division fluency, useful strategies and progress. The separate printable game materials and publisher-gated reflection Cool-down are unverified.
Source-authentic activity scripts are teacher mediated. Figures, print-only masters and publisher-gated Cool-downs not independently inspected are not claimed source-identical.

KeyConcepts.Title: Division by known factors
KeyConcepts.Definition: Find quotient using a related multiplication fact.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Check divisor times quotient equals dividend.

KeyConcepts.Title: Race to 1
KeyConcepts.Definition: Select a new starting number or an earlier quotient and divide by a rolled divisor.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Reroll a 5; record actual moves; reach quotient 1 to win.

KeyConcepts.Title: Compare Division
KeyConcepts.Definition: Compare the quotients on two revealed division expression cards.
KeyConcepts.Rule: The higher numeric quotient wins both cards.

WorkedExamples.Question: Show a valid path starting with 12, using divisors 3 then 4.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Allowing a rolled divisor of five in Race to 1.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The source specifically requires rerolling a five.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Using a brand-new starter number on all turns and ignoring previous quotients.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Later turns allow either starter number or previous quotient.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Explain which number was chosen and why.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Choosing the greater dividend without computing the card quotient.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Compare Division ranks quotients, not dividends.
